mandatoryFindings.issue: The new operative sentence says STUDIO_DISPATCHER_ENABLED=false disables both schedulers, but the captured worker profile defines studio.execution.dispatcher.enabled=true literally. The alias is referenced only by the lower packaged application.yml property; rendering the alias into the worker environment is not proof that the worker profile consumes it.
mandatoryFindings.impact: An operator can mistake a rendered alias for an effective stop or diagnose a healthy active worker as unable to dispatch/reap. This is a source-configuration inference, not an inspected process result.
mandatoryFindings.smallestCorrection: State that effective studio.execution.dispatcher.enabled=false disables the scheduler beans. Distinguish the chart-rendered STUDIO_DISPATCHER_ENABLED alias from that effective property; disclose the literal worker-profile override and require effective-property verification. Do not prescribe a new code/config fix or claim deployed behavior. Reconcile the section5 audit row accordingly.

mandatoryFindings.issue: The retained operative rollback warning still says turning off the dispatcher leaves queued work until its deadline. When the effective dispatcher property is false, StudioRecoveryScheduler is also disabled, so passage of the deadline does not itself close rows. This contradicts the newly corrected sections5/6.
mandatoryFindings.impact: Rollback instructions imply automatic deadline closure even after the component that performs it has been disabled.
mandatoryFindings.smallestCorrection: Replace “until its deadline” with “until a scheduler resumes and performs closure/reaping”; retain the instruction to leave the dispatcher enabled while engaging the execution kill switch. No source change.

mandatoryFindings.issue: The retained current security statement says any of the three bypasses makes Studio authorization use whatever identity the caller wrote in a header. Only identity-headers accepts X-User-* input. With that flag closed, core-service returns a fixed administrative identity; csi-read augments an already resolved identity only for CSI GETs and does not authenticate Studio writes from headers.
mandatoryFindings.impact: The audited runbook collapses three distinct authorization effects and contradicts its own corrected section9 table and warning.
mandatoryFindings.smallestCorrection: Qualify the header-identity statement specifically to identity-headers; describe the fixed core-service admin bypass and CSI-GET-only role augmentation separately or refer to the already-correct section9 table. Preserve ED-02 and its real-identity proof gap. No authorization change.
